text.p: 50-Off Stores Inc on Wednesday said it received U.S. Bankruptcy Court approval to proceed with its Chapter 11 reorganization plan.
The company, which will be changing its name to Lot$Off Corp, said the plan calls for:
-- a substantial reduction in principal and a lengthening of maturity of long-term debt;
-- the cancelation of all outstanding common stock, warrants and options;
-- the issuance to general unsecured creditors of 770,170 shares of Series B preferred stock valued at about $3.99 each.
-- the issuance to general unsecured creditors of 770,170 shares of Series B preferred stock valued at about $3.99 million and convertible into two shares of Lot$Off common stock;
-- the forgiveness of more than $28 million of pre-petition obligations of the company; and
-- the sale of at least 30,500 units, each comprising 20 shares of Series A preferred stock and 20 shares of Lott$Off common stock, at $100 per unit.
The company said it had received subscriptions for 44,736 units as of May 30.

The company also said General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp unit has agreed to supply up to $15 million in senior secured exit financing required under the plan, which takes effect June 16.
Earlier, the company closed 60 of its 101 stores. It now operates 41 core outlets in Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, New Mexico and Tennessee.
Charles Fuhrmann, 50-Off president, chief executive and chief financial officer, will become chairman of a new board of directors while continuing in his current posts, it said.
